claims.text: Published 5 June 2023 by Leslie Kean and Ralph Blumenthal with named on-record corroboration from Karl Nell and Christopher Mellon and pseudonymous corroboration from a serving NASIC officer.
Reports Grusch's claim that the retrieved material includes intact and partially intact vehicles with unique atomic arrangements and radiological signatures.
Reports that Grusch left government on 7 April 2023 to advance accountability through public disclosure, and that he helped draft the UAP whistleblower language in the FY2023 NDAA.

desc: The article that made Grusch public. Written by Leslie Kean and Ralph Blumenthal - the same reporting pair behind the December 2017 New York Times AATIP story - and published by The Debrief on 5 June 2023 after major national outlets passed on it. Its architecture is what made it durable: rather than resting on Grusch alone, it carries on-record corroboration from retired Army Col. Karl Nell, the Army's UAP Task Force liaison, who calls Grusch beyond reproach and affirms the eighty-year reverse-engineering arms race as fundamentally correct; from Christopher Mellon, former Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Intelligence, on well-placed officials sharing detailed information; and from a serving NASIC officer under the name Jonathan Grey. It documents the July 2021 DoD IG disclosure, the May 2022 ICIG filing by McCullough, the July 2022 credible-and-urgent determination, and the April 2023 DOPSR clearances. Grusch's core claims as reported: intact and partially intact vehicles of non-human origin have been retrieved for decades; the materials have unique atomic arrangements and radiological signatures; the activity is illegally withheld from Congress by nesting inside classified programs; and individuals inside those programs raised concerns about illegal contracting.
